audit_findings.title: FY2025 consolidated OE does not match ARKO's post-IPO economic claim
audit_findings.magnitude: APC minority claim was 24.1% at IPO and 26.4% by June 30, 2026; six-month 2026 net income attributable to noncontrolling interests was $4.365 million and noncontrolling-interest equity was $68.700 million; exact OE and cash-bridge effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The $13.0 million anchor and consolidated cash/STI include 100% of APC, although ARKO common owns only 73.6% of APC after the underwriters' exercise; APC standalone-company costs also reduce post-IPO earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: We currently own 75.9% of the economic interests and 94.0% of the combined voting power of APC.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch and is material relative to the small OE anchor. The filings establish that minority investors now own part of APC's earnings and net assets, but they do not provide enough information to allocate FY2025 OE or June 2026 cash between ARKO and the minority accurately.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct FY2025 OE by legal entity or segment, apply ARKO's 73.6% economic ownership to APC cash flows and APC-held cash/STI, include recurring APC standalone costs, and rerun all scenarios and the bridge.

audit_findings.title: The $100 million redeemable preferred claim is absent from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $100.000 million redemption value, equal to 23.4% of the $427 million base equity value and $0.73 per current diluted share; FY2025 preferred dividends were $5.750 million, or 44.2% of the $13.0 million anchor; 8.703 million conversion shares were disclosed at June 30, 2026, plus up to 1.2 million bonus shares
audit_findings.mechanism: A redemption outcome requires deducting the senior preferred claim and retaining preferred dividends in common-level OE while removing conversion dilution; a conversion outcome keeps the capital in equity and includes conversion dilution but eliminates future preferred dividends.
audit_findings.evidence: At any time on or after August 31, 2027, holders of at least a majority of the then outstanding shares of the Series A Stock or the Company may deliver written notice requesting or notifying of redemption of all or a portion of shares of the Series A Stock at a price equal to the Liquidation Preference (as defined below).
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge demonstrably omits a filed $100 million senior claim while the share count apparently includes preferred-related dilution. Holding the existing denominator constant, a simple $100 million deduction would reduce base value from $3.11 to about $2.38 per share. That is not a valid final rerun until the included shares and dividend treatment are traced, because the current hybrid can overstate value through the omitted claim and understate it through dilution that would not exist upon redemption.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $13.0 million OE anchor to confirm whether the $5.750 million preferred dividend was deducted, reconcile every component of the 137.062221 million diluted shares, and rerun separate coherent redemption and conversion cases.

audit_findings.title: Recurring transformation and acquisition payroll may have been stripped as a one-off
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 acquisition and divestiture add-back was $6.545 million, equal to 50.3% of the $13.0 million anchor; the recurring payroll and dealerization portions are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If OE adopted the Adjusted EBITDA exclusion, dedicated M&A, integration and dealerization payroll would have been added back despite being recurring operating compensation, inflating the OE anchor and every projected year.
audit_findings.evidence: (a) Eliminates costs incurred that are directly attributable to business acquisitions and divestitures (including conversion of retail stores to dealer locations) and salaries of employees whose primary job function is to execute our acquisition and divestiture strategy and facilitate integration of acquired operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the non-GAAP add-back includes employee salaries and costs associated with continuing strategies, but the supplied record does not show that the OE calculation used this add-back or how much of the $6.545 million was recurring. The possible effect is large, but materiality cannot be established without that split and the OE worksheet.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $13.0 million anchor line by line to GAAP results and obtain the $6.545 million account-level schedule; retain dedicated payroll and recurring dealerization/integration costs, remove only identified nonrecurring transaction costs, and rerun if any amount was excluded.

audit_findings.title: Asset-retirement cash obligations may be missing from owner earnings and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: ARO was $89.892 million at December 31, 2025 and approximately $90.3 million at June 30, 2026; cash settlements were $0.604 million in FY2025 and $0.357 million in first-half 2026; normalized uncovered amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Tank-removal settlements reduce the ARO liability rather than property-purchase capex and therefore can be omitted when OE adds back depreciation or accretion without deducting settlement cash; alternatively, an uncovered ARO claim may require a bridge reserve.
audit_findings.evidence: The future cost to remove a storage tank is recognized over the estimated remaining useful life of the storage tank, or if sooner, the termination of the applicable lease.
audit_findings.explanation: A substantial filed obligation exists, but deducting the entire discounted ARO from the bridge would double count costs if OE already contains an adequate normalized cash allowance. Actual FY2025 settlements were only 4.6% of the anchor, while future timing and reimbursements are not established, so the record cannot determine the sustainable annual charge or uncovered bridge amount.
audit_findings.action: Map ARO accretion, related asset depreciation, retirement settlements and reimbursements into the OE worksheet; develop a filed asset-level settlement schedule and then either deduct normalized settlement cash from OE or reserve the non-duplicative uncovered obligation in the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Finance-lease principal may disappear when depreciation is added back
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 finance-lease principal was $5.704 million, equal to 43.9% of the $13.0 million anchor; if omitted and treated as recurring, the computed base-value reduction is approximately $75.9 million or $0.55 per diluted share; first-half 2026 principal was $10.028 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back finance-lease ROU-asset depreciation while deducting only cash purchases of property and equipment excludes principal repayments from OE even though they finance recurring operating assets.
audit_findings.evidence: For the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, total cash outflows for leases amounted to approximately $ 184.7 million , $ 180.5 million and $ 171.9 million for operating leases, respectively, and $ 22.3 million , $ 22.2 million and $ 22.3 million for financing leases, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is not demonstrated without the OE worksheet, but the filed principal payments establish that the potential error is material. The conditional base impact would reduce value from about $3.11 to $2.56 per share before any tax or replacement-capital refinements.
audit_findings.action: Trace finance-lease depreciation and the $5.704 million principal payment through FY2025 OE, reconcile lease-financed asset additions against maintenance capex, deduct principal or an equivalent replacement-capital charge if absent, and rerun all scenarios.
